children: European natural-gas prices are at their highest since the end of 2022 as low inventory levels and LNG disruptions in the Middle East raise concerns over winter supply. In early trading, the benchmark Dutch TTF contract is flat at 79.21 euros a megawatt-hour after breaching 80 euros in the previous session. The biggest concern is Europe's storage position. EU gas inventories are around 67% full, significantly below the 84% five-year average. With the next heating season approaching, the European gas market is more exposed to supply disruptions and renewed price volatility. A widening spread between TTF and JKM prices--the benchmark price for spot LNG in Asia--is also adding support, as stronger LNG prices in Asia increase competition for cargoes and could make it more difficult for Europe to attract sufficient supply. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
